title: Purpose of migrations
body: What do EF Core migrations provide?

options.t: Automatic backups
Versioned, incremental schema changes generated from the model and applied to the database
Data replication
Query caching

answer: A versioned history of schema changes derived from the model.
explanation: `dotnet ef migrations add Name` compares the model with the last snapshot and generates Up/Down code. Apply with `dotnet ef database update`, `Database.MigrateAsync()`, or generate idempotent SQL scripts for production pipelines.

title: The N+1 query problem
body: A page lists 50 orders and, for each one, accesses `order.Customer.Name` with lazy loading enabled. What happens?

options.t: One query loads everything
1 query for the orders plus up to 50 additional queries for customers (N+1)
The code throws
EF caches customers automatically, so no extra queries

answer: N+1 queries; fix with Include or a projection.
explanation: Use eager loading (`Include(o => o.Customer)`) or, better, project only the needed columns: `.Select(o => new { o.Id, CustomerName = o.Customer.Name })`, which becomes a single JOIN.

title: AsNoTracking

options.t: Always, for every query
For read-only queries whose results will not be updated via SaveChanges
Only for inserts
To enable lazy loading

explanation: Tracking stores snapshots for change detection, which costs memory and CPU. Read-only endpoints benefit from `AsNoTracking()` or projections to DTOs (which are never tracked).

title: Untranslatable predicates
body: What does EF Core 3.0+ do when a `Where` predicate calls a C# method it cannot translate to SQL?

options.t: Silently loads the whole table and filters in memory
options.e: That was EF Core 2.x client evaluation behaviour.

options.t: Throws an InvalidOperationException explaining the expression could not be translated
Ignores the predicate
Translates it to a stored procedure

explanation: Since 3.0, client evaluation is only allowed in the final projection. Rewrite the predicate with translatable expressions, or explicitly switch to client evaluation with `AsEnumerable()` after reducing the data set.

title: DbContext lifetime
body: Which statement about `DbContext` in ASP.NET Core is correct?

options.t: It is thread-safe and should be a singleton
It is not thread-safe; register it scoped (per request) and do not run parallel operations on one instance
It must be created with new in every method
It can only be used synchronously

explanation: `AddDbContext` registers it as scoped. Starting two queries concurrently on the same context throws. Use `IDbContextFactory` for background jobs or Blazor Server, and `AddDbContextPool` to reduce allocation overhead.

title: Preventing SQL injection in ADO.NET
body: How should user input be included in an ADO.NET `SqlCommand`?

options.t: Concatenate it after escaping single quotes
Use SqlParameter objects (e.g. @email) instead of string concatenation
Base64-encode it
Wrap it in square brackets

explanation: Parameters are sent separately from the SQL text, so input is never interpreted as SQL, and plans can be reused. Dapper and EF Core parameterise automatically (EF's `FromSqlInterpolated`/`SqlQuery` convert interpolated values into parameters).
